assessment.headline: DAY 32. BW Tyr docked Mumbai. But Trump may accept Hormuz staying closed. 4 IDF killed. Haifa hit. The war is reshaping.
assessment.body:
The most consequential signal today: Bloomberg reports Trump is willing to end the war even if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. If true, this fundamentally changes everything — it means the US may stop fighting but India's energy crisis could become PERMANENT, with Iran controlling Hormuz toll fees indefinitely.

Meanwhile, the war intensified on every front: Iran struck Haifa oil refineries (smoke visible across northern Israel). A fully laden Kuwaiti tanker was hit near Dubai. 4 Israeli soldiers were killed in a single Hezbollah clash — the deadliest incident. 3 Indonesian UN peacekeepers were killed. 2 Chinese COSCO mega-ships turned around at Larak Island. And an Indian worker was killed in a Kuwait strike — India's first confirmed civilian casualty in the Gulf.

But India's Hormuz pipeline continues: BW Tyr docked at Mumbai today with LPG. BW Elm reaches Mangalore tomorrow. 8 carriers have now crossed safely, delivering ~450,000+ MT of fuel. 18 ships + 485 crew remain.

Verified India snapshot (Day 32, 6 PM):
• Sensex 71,948 — worst month in 6 years. Nifty 22,331
• Rupee 94.84 ATL. FII $12.3B outflow — all-time record
• 8 carriers crossed Hormuz. BW Tyr at Mumbai today
• 18 ships + 485 crew remain. 942+ seafarers repatriated
• Indian worker killed in Kuwait — first Gulf casualty
• Excise cut ₹10/L. Indian basket $125/bbl
• Iran missiles slowed to 10-15/day (from 90 on day 1)

April 6 = 6 days. Pakistan hosting talks. Israel says NO scaling back. The Bloomberg report on Hormuz is the signal to watch — if confirmed, India must prepare for a world where Hormuz is permanently controlled by Iran, not reopened by force.
